newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T up after tobacco settlement reports.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T up after tobacco settlement reports.

text.p: B.A.T Industries Plc shares rose early on Monday amid further press comment on the possibility of legal moves by the industry in the U.S. to settle claims over smoking-related diseases.

The Sunday Telegraph said B.A.T had proposed a $3 billion fighting fund across the industry to cushion against rising legal costs, while a report in the Times said B.A.T was under pressure to bring forward a demerger of its tobacco and financial services operations.
The stock was up 3-1/2p at 497-1/2 by 0820 GMT in volume of 127,600 shares.
In an unsourced report, the Times said B.A.T was believed to have decided that a demerger could take place by the end of the year.
No-one from the company was immediately available for comment.
B.A.T on Friday dismissed a decision by rival Ligett Group to settle U.S. tobacco litigation, saying the move would not force it to seek a similar pact.
However, chief executive Martin Broughton said at the time of the company's results earlier this month it could be time to explore ways of settling the claims because of the mounting costs.
